questions.q: What is the capstone project described in this lesson?
options: A single one-off API request script with no conversation history
A fine-tuned custom model trained from scratch
A real, multi-turn command-line chat application that maintains history and streams replies
A static slide deck summarizing the course
questions.explain: The capstone is a genuine multi-turn conversation loop — message history maintained across turns, with streamed replies — not a single blocking request.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does the application need to resend the full message history on every single turn?
options: Because the API requires exactly one message per request and nothing more
Because the model has no memory between calls — Chapter 1's point about how LLMs actually work
Because streaming requires re-sending history for technical reasons unrelated to memory
It doesn't need to — history is optional and rarely used in practice
questions.explain: As Chapter 1 established, the model has no memory of its own between API calls — the full messages array is how a conversation's context is provided every time.

questions.q: Which chapter does this lesson say is directly responsible for the core techniques (chat completions, roles, streaming) used in the capstone build?
options: Chapter 1
Chapter 2
Chapter 3
Chapter 5
questions.explain: Chapter 3 (Working With LLM APIs) covers chat completions, roles, and streaming — the exact three lessons this project assembles into one working loop.

questions.q: According to the lesson, why is fine-tuning NOT part of this capstone build?
options: A good system prompt accomplishes the persona/behavior goal instead, per Chapter 4's 'prompt first' guidance
Fine-tuning is impossible with the Messages API
Fine-tuning is only available for image models, not chat models
The capstone doesn't involve any kind of prompting at all
questions.explain: Chapter 4 established that prompting (including a well-designed system prompt) should come before fine-tuning — the capstone uses a system prompt to define its persona instead of training a custom model.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four rubric requirements for the finished capstone build?
options: It must support image generation
It must be written in a language other than Python
It must avoid using any system prompt
It must use stream: true so replies print incrementally rather than all at once
questions.explain: The four rubric points are: a growing message history, streamed replies (stream: true), a defined system prompt/persona, and a clean way to exit — streaming is explicitly required.
